learning_outcomes.text: Question the physical and mathematical foundations.
Assemble a toolbox for the analysis of electronic circuits.
Understand the functioning of selected electronic components including their representation by equivalent circuits.
Students acquire a basic understanding of how electronic circuits are analyzed, calculated and designed.

syllabus_topics: Physics: Energy, potential, voltage, current, Ohm's law, power.
Mathematics: Node and mesh equations, linear two-ports, useful simplifications, controlled sources, components with nonlinear characteristics.
Tools: Resistor networks, voltage dividers, current dividers, decomposition into superpositions, two-port simplification.
Diodes: LED display for logic values, rectifiers, diode as voltage source, logic functions.
Circuits with bipolar transistors: Voltage amplifiers, differential amplifiers, current sources, transistor inverters, DT gates, voltage stabilization.
MOS transistors: Amplifiers, switching operation, CMOS gates, memory cells.
Operational amplifiers: Amplifiers, computing elements, comparator, analog-to-digital converter.
Capacitance, inductance, mutual inductance, dirt effects.
Time-discrete model: Principle, smoothing capacitor, switching power supply, H-bridge, CMOS inverter.
Switched systems: Step response, switched RC element, mapping to RC elements, switched RL element, mapping to RL elements, RC oscillator.
Frequency domain: Fourier transform, FFT/Matlab, complex U, I, R, mapping of circuits to equation systems, tools, transistor amplifiers, operational amplifiers.
Semiconductors: Movable electrons, conductors and non-conductors, doped semiconductors.
pn-junction: Voltage-free, depletion region, forward region.
MOS transistor: Field effect, active region, pinch-off region.
Lines: Wave equation, characteristic impedance, reflection, step response, measuring line parameters.
assessment_rules: The assessment is a written exam (90 minutes) if there are more than 9 participants, otherwise an oral examination (30 minutes). Homework assignments for Electronics I are a mandatory prerequisite for the exam, but are ungraded and have 0% weight.
